title: NEW MSFS Marketplace Additions: 4 Incredible General Aviation Airports Analyzed!
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator marketplace just loaded up a phenomenal collection of diverse destinations this week! Whether you want to land at a rugged backcountry strip, tackle challenging island approaches in the Caribbean, or explore beautifully updated regional gateways in the UK, there is an adventure waiting for your virtual hangar.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we split today's major releases into two logical groups to see which environments genuinely deserve a spot on your virtual flight logs:

✈️ US REGIONAL & BACKCOUNTRY HUBS: We kick things off with a rugged beauty in Northern California—Happy Camp Airport (36S) by ORBX. This incredible scenery pack invites you to navigate the stunning canyons, valleys, and sandbars of the magnificent lower Klamath River. It’s a true heaven for bush pilots and short take-off and landing (STOL) machines! To wrap up the United States group, we check out the Spirit of St. Louis Airport (KSUS) by MSFSScenery builders, located in Chesterfield, Missouri, featuring updated aprons, custom ground vehicles, and newly added support buildings.

🌏 INTERNATIONAL ISLAND & COASTAL GATEWAYS: Next, we head across the Atlantic to look at Gamston Airport (EGNE) by Burning Blue Design. This vital transition point in the north of England features 80 custom 3D objects, full PBR physical-based rendering textures, and a highly accurate layout including the main control tower and apron cafe. Finally, we journey to the Bahamas to explore Marsh Harbour Airport (MYAM)—a key destination for regional airlines and island hopping. This highly detailed rendition includes fully modeled interiors for the terminal and Cherokee Aviation hangar, alongside fantastic realistic wear and tear on the ATC tower.

Which of these environments are you adding to your flight routes first? Are you planning to take a bush plane out to the mountains of California, or will you be loading up a twin prop for a relaxing island flight over the Bahamas? Let me know in the comments below!

If this structured marketplace breakdown helped you plan your next route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism and scenery updates!
